antidotes.why: Today's effort; only with yv.2.6.21 alongside.
Doing beats not doing; steadiness comes from acting.
Steadiness keeps the best from abandoning what they began.

chains.summary: Fate is only one's own earlier effort. Today's effort and yesterday's meet like two rams, and the stronger wins, so make today's the stronger. A tired mind says that fate did it. Whatever you practise, you become.
chains.title: Fate is your own past effort

verses.m: Past effort and present effort fight like two rams, sometimes evenly matched and sometimes not; the weaker one gives way. So strive by every means, with skill and good application, so that today's effort quickly wins.
verses.sa: द्वौ हुडाविव युध्येते पुरुषार्थौ समासमौ । प्राक्तनश्चैहिकश्चैव शाम्यत्यत्राल्पवीर्यवान् ॥ अतः पुरुषयत्नेन यतितव्यं यथा तथा । पुंसा तन्त्रेण सद्योगाद्येनाश्वद्यतनो जयेत् ॥

verses.m: There is no doubt: past faults are calmed by present virtues. The proof is that yesterday's mistake is undone by today's good deeds.
verses.sa: दोषः शाम्यत्यसंदेहं प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनैर्गुणैः । दृष्टान्तोऽत्र ह्यस्तनस्य दोषस्याद्य गुणैः क्षयः ॥

verses.m: As the effort, so quickly comes the fruit. So there is only effort; if you want to call it fate, it is that same effort.
verses.sa: यथा यथा प्रयत्नः स्याद्भवेदाशु फलं तथा । इति पौरुषमेवास्ति दैवमस्तु तदेव च ॥

chains.summary: The joy one grows into by practice, like poison first and nectar in the end, is born of a clear understanding of the self. Pleasure from the senses is nectar first and poison after. The pleasure of sleep, laziness and heedlessness deludes from start to finish.
chains.title: Poison first, nectar after

verses.m: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
verses.sa: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥

verses.m: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
verses.sa: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥

verses.m: The happiness that comes from contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called rajasic.
verses.sa: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥

chains.summary: Sattva produces knowledge. Rajas produces greed. Tamas produces heedlessness, delusion and ignorance. Tamas binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep. When rajas rules there is greed, restless activity and craving.
chains.title: What each guna yields

verses.m: Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep, Bharata.
verses.sa: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥

verses.m: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
verses.sa: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥

verses.m: Darkness, inertia, heedlessness and delusion: these arise when tamas increases, joy of the Kurus.
verses.sa: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥

chains.summary: The low do not begin because they fear obstacles. The middling begin, then stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
chains.title: Three kinds of people before an obstacle

verses.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
verses.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

depicts.m: He drags out what needs doing, doubts everything, and is slow where speed is needed: such a person is a fool, best of the Bharatas.
depicts.sa: संसारयति कृत्यानि सर्वत्र विचिकित्सते / चिरं करोति क्षिप्रार्थे स मूढो भरतर्षभ
depicts.why: Depicts stretching out what needs doing.

gloss: Heaviness that keeps one from beginning. Bhartrihari: the great enemy living in one's own body.

heals.m: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
heals.sa: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥

heals.m: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
heals.sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
heals.why: Shows doing the work that is yours is better than waiting, and even living needs action.

heals.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
heals.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥
heals.why: Shows not starting as the lowest option.

heals.m: When one acts, one becomes steadfast. One does not become steadfast without acting; only by acting does one become steadfast. So action itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand action.'
heals.sa: यदा वै करोत्यथ निस्तिष्ठति नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति कृतिस्त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्येति कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
heals.why: Shows waiting to feel steady before acting is the wrong order.

heals.m: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
heals.sa: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥

heals.m: Whoever wants something and works for it step by step will surely get it, unless they turn back halfway.
heals.sa: यो यमर्थं प्रार्थयते तदर्थं चेहते क्रमात् । अवश्यं स तमाप्नोति न चेदर्धान्निवर्तते ॥
heals.why: Names the only failure as stopping halfway.

heals.m: There is no doubt: past faults are calmed by present virtues. The proof is that yesterday's mistake is undone by today's good deeds.
heals.sa: दोषः शाम्यत्यसंदेहं प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनैर्गुणैः । दृष्टान्तोऽत्र ह्यस्तनस्य दोषस्याद्य गुणैः क्षयः ॥

heals.m: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
heals.sa: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
heals.why: Shows early discipline marks lasting happiness, not a reason to stop.

hero.m: The doer who is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating, is called tamasic.
hero.sa: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥

loci.m: The doer who is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating, is called tamasic.
loci.sa: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥

loci.m: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
loci.sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥

loci.m: Laziness is the great enemy that lives in a person's own body. There is no friend like effort; one who works does not sink.
loci.sa: आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महारिपुः । नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कुर्वाणो नावसीदति ॥

practices.m: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
practices.why: Bearing what passes without being moved.

practices.m: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
practices.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
practices.why: Shows wisdom staying set when the senses are gathered.

practices.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
practices.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
practices.why: Cultivates the capacity to hold steady while the surge passes.

practices.m: The lowest do not begin at all, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles strike. The best, struck by obstacles again and again, do not give up what they have begun.
practices.sa: प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ॥ विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः प्रारब्धमुत्तमगुणा न परित्यजन्ति ॥

practices.m: Laziness is the great enemy that lives in a person's own body. There is no friend like effort; one who works does not sink.
practices.sa: आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महारिपुः । नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कुर्वाणो नावसीदति ॥

practices.m: When pain of body or mind arrives and nothing can be done about it, do not keep thinking about it. Not dwelling on it is the medicine for sorrow; brooding does not make it leave, it only makes it grow.
practices.sa: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् / चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते / यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत्
practices.why: Shows withholding attention from the loop as the practice.

practices.m: If an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself over it. Keep applying yourself again and again; this is the highest rule for those who lead.
practices.sa: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः
practices.why: Shows renewed exertion is called the supreme rule.

practices.m: Never give up what is right out of desire, rage or hatred. Don't be overjoyed by what pleases you, nor burn with distress at what does not.
practices.sa: न च कामान्न संरम्भान्न द्वेषाद्धर्ममुत्सृजेत् / प्रिये नातिभृशं हृष्येदप्रिये न च संज्वरेत्
practices.why: Holding to dharma under pull is shown.

stories.l: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
stories.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.

stories.l: Sometimes we need someone else to remind us what we can do; and the old can be that someone.
stories.s: Nobody can leap the ocean. Old Jambavant admits honestly that he is no longer young. Then he turns to the silent Hanuman and asks why he sits quiet: what task in the world is too hard for him? Hanuman grows to the size of a mountain.
stories.t: Jambavant reminds Hanuman of his strength

stories.l: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.
stories.s: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
stories.t: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is

stories.l: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.
stories.s: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
stories.t: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
